THE DESTINATION

About Kedarnath Temple

Kedarnath Temple is one of the most sacred Hindu temples dedicated to Lord Shiva, located in the Garhwal Himalayas near the origin of the Mandakini River at an altitude of about 3,583 metres (11,755 ft). It is an important part of the Char Dham and is also among the five sacred temples of Panch Kedar.

According to Hindu mythology, the temple was originally built by the Pandavas after the Mahabharata war and later revived by Adi Shankaracharya. Surrounded by majestic snow-covered Himalayan peaks, Kedarnath attracts thousands of pilgrims and trekkers every year who undertake a challenging trek of around 16–18 km from Gaurikund to seek blessings and experience the spiritual beauty of the Himalayas.

REASONS TO GO

Why Visit Kedarnath

Spiritual significance — Kedarnath is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva, a deeply sacred place for devotees seeking blessings and peace.

Breathtaking Himalayan views — the temple is surrounded by snow-covered peaks including Kedarnath Peak.

Memorable trekking experience — the 16–18 km trek from Gaurikund winds through scenic valleys, waterfalls, and Himalayan landscapes.

Peaceful & spiritual atmosphere — temple bells and the evening aarti create a vibe many visitors describe as life-changing.

Gateway to other sacred places — nearby Bhairavnath Temple adds more to the journey.

Cultural exploration — visit ancient temples in Guptkashi en route.

Safety first — medical kits, oxygen, and experienced trek leaders throughout.

DAY BY DAY

Your Itinerary

  • Start Time: 6:00 AM pickup from Haridwar Bus Station.
  • Scenic Drive: 225 km / ~8 hrs through Rishikesh, Devprayag, and Rudraprayag.
  • Devprayag Sangam: Stop where the Alaknanda meets the Bhagirathi to form the Ganga.
  • Evening Visit: Vishwanath Temple & Ardh Narishwar Temple in Guptkashi (optional).
  • Overnight Stay: Hotel / guesthouse in Sitapur.
  • Meals: Dinner.
  • Early Morning Drive: Sitapur to Gaurikund (~5 km / 30 mins).
  • Trek Begins: 16 km uphill trek to Kedarnath (pony/palki/heli available at extra cost).
  • En Route: Witness stunning mountain views, the Mandakini river, and spiritual surroundings.
  • Darshan: Visit Kedarnath Temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas.
  • Overnight Stay: Guesthouse / hotel near Kedarnath.
  • Meals: Breakfast & dinner.
  • Morning: Temple visit & breakfast.
  • Descend: 16 km trek back down to Gaurikund.
  • Drive Back: To Sitapur and check-in.
  • Evening: Free for rest or exploring nearby.
  • Meals: Breakfast & dinner.
  • After Breakfast: Drive back 225 km to Haridwar.
  • Journey Ends: With spiritual memories.
  • Meal: Breakfast.

  • Travel insurance or personal medical coverage
  • Porter charges during the trek
  • Special pujas, VIP darshan, or donations
